title: Trunk training: does the crossing survive when both families train their own representation?

device._note: The sparse whitening stays on numpy CPU (M107's arithmetic, validated to reproduce M107 at 8.7e-05 by the M108 pre-seal check); everything trainable runs on the GPU (torch device 'cuda' = ROCm/HIP here). HIP_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1 is a precondition; device_count must be 1 and gcnArchName gfx1201.

parity_guard.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens
parity_guard._note: plan section 4.6.1. Every sealed v16 run re-runs the parity check at startup (onnxruntime CPU session against torch cuda, same fixed input, M107's feature definition) and a run whose worst relative disagreement exceeds 1e-04 is VOID, not negative. The bound is ~8x the measured 1.263e-05.

dense.feature: CLS token concatenated with the mean of the patch tokens
_resolution_note: REGISTERED DESIGN DECISION, 6 August 2026. Dense trunk training runs at resolutions {28, 42, 224}: 28 (analytic 107.6M MACs) and 42 (215.6M) bracket the two M107 crossing budgets where the crossing lives; 224 is the in-distribution operating point. The rest of M107's frozen resolution sweep (56, 70, 98, 140) remains in the sealed M107 curve as the t1 frozen reference and is not re-trained. Training at 28/42 is cheap (4 and 9 tokens) and is exactly the regime where the crossing is contested.
Each resolution is a separate model instance (as in M107, each resolution was a separate arm); they do not share trained weights across resolutions.
dense._feature_note: M107's published linear-evaluation feature, unchanged, so the frozen rung reproduces M107.

_best_arm_note: REGISTERED DESIGN DECISION, 6 August 2026. Plan section 5.2 says the t1 sparse rung is 'M108's best arm, frozen'. M108 showed no construction beats arm (a) meaningfully (arm (c) beats arm (a) at 1 of 6 budgets by +0.28pp, mean c-a ~ -0.11pp), so 'best' is read as the highest-accuracy sparse arm: arm (a) generalist at 3072 atoms (0.2153), which also reproduces M107 exactly (8.7e-05) — making the t1 sparse rung a reproduction of the sealed frozen ladder rather than a new object.
The dictionary is the 3072 x 108 whitened-patch array from M108's arm (a) construction; at t3 it becomes a trainable parameter, at t4 the whitener (mean and 108x108 whiten) becomes trainable too.

schedule._note: plan section 5.2 restriction 1: fixed before the first run, identical across families; per-family learning-rate scale is permitted and registered here as equal. A scale change is a re-registration, never a silent tune.
schedule._t1_note: t1 (frozen) is NOT trained with this schedule: it reproduces M107/M108 via the closed-form ridge head, exactly as the frozen rung is defined.

head._note: t1 uses the closed-form multi-output ridge at the M107 constant (1.0) so the frozen rung reproduces the sealed figures. t2-t4 train a 345-way linear head with the shared schedule on BOTH families (same optimiser, epochs, LR shape, early stopping).

t3_partial.dense: LoRA rank 16 on qkv+out projections, last-2 blocks unfrozen, head trained
t3_partial.sparse: dictionary gradient-trained (0.33M), whitener frozen, head trained

t4_full.dense: full fine-tune of the trunk, head trained
t4_full.sparse: dictionary and whitener both trained, head trained

t4_from_scratch_dense.dense: DINOv2-small geometry, random init, same schedule, 224px

gate.registered_prediction: The dense side gains more from trunk training than the sparse side does, and the M107 crossings close. A 21.46M-parameter transformer pre-trained on 142M images has more capacity to reallocate toward 345 classes than a 3072-atom dictionary of 6x6 patches has. Written against the program's interest and now aligned with the literature (Ghorbani et al. 2020; Szekely et al. 2024).
gate.kill_switch_1: If the dense curve is above the sparse curve at every overlapping MAC budget once both trunks are trained, M107's crossing does not survive trunk training; the admissible reading of M107 narrows to 'frozen sparse features beat frozen out-of-distribution dense features at two budgets on one corpus'. Headline under plan section 3.6.
gate.kill_switch_2: If the sparse side is still above the dense side somewhere after both trunks are trained, the crossing is a property of the representation rather than of the freezing; the claim is bounded to those budgets, that corpus and the accuracy quoted beside them.
gate.kill_switch_3: If trunk training does not move the sparse curve at all (the gradient-trained dictionary matches the constructed one), the sparse dictionary is at capacity, not at its optimum, and every future sparse gain must come from more atoms or better construction rather than from optimisation.
gate._comparison_rule: A sparse point at M MACs is compared against the best dense point at or below M MACs (M107 gate, unchanged). Each rung reports its frozen predecessor beside it (plan section 5.2 restriction 2).
gate._t4_inversion_disclosure: At t4 the sparse side is trained on the evaluation corpus while the (t4) dense trunk is either LVD-142M pre-trained or, in the from-scratch arm, trained on the corpus from random init. The from-scratch arm is the §5.2.6 symmetry resolution: at least one t4 comparison pairs two models that have seen exactly the same data and nothing else. Without that arm, no t4 figure is entitled.

numerics._note: float32 training, float64 normal equations where the closed-form ridge is used. torch.manual_seed(109) for the from-scratch init and any stochastic sampling.
